office_does: The auditor runs county elections, records deeds and other documents, licenses vehicles and vessels, and keeps the county's financial accounts and reports.
race_blurb: Auditor Shoona Riggs, in office since 2015 after decades in the Clallam and Jefferson auditor's offices, faces Sequim attorney Virginia Shogren, who runs on election integrity and cutting waste. They disagree over the state of the voter rolls and ballot chain of custody.

candidates.summary: Sequim attorney and former U.S. Patent and Trademark Office attorney running to 'restore trust in our elections' with hand-countable paper ballots and to cut county waste.
highlights: Calls for 'paper ballots you can watch and count' and says the county voter list 'is a mess' [S1][S5]
Pledges to watch 'every county expense closely' and cut waste; cited DOGE in her forum opening [S1][S5]
Opposes ranked-choice voting; supports consolidating elections to once a year [S5]
Sanctioned by the state Supreme Court in 2022 over a petition alleging noncitizen voter registration [S6]

spending.basis: Pledges to watch every county expense, cut waste and spend less so 'more money stays in your pocket,' and frames waste through DOGE.

experience.basis: Challenger from private legal practice with no county administrative experience, running to change how elections are run.

candidates.summary: Clallam County Auditor since 2015, formerly chief deputy auditor and elections supervisor, with 36 years in the Clallam and Jefferson auditor's offices.
highlights: 36 years in county auditor's offices; Washington State Certified Election Administrator since 1999 [S1]
Endorsed by Secretary of State Steve Hobbs and county auditors; cites support from former Secretary of State Kim Wyman [S1]
Disputed her opponent's voter-roll and chain-of-custody claims; supports once-a-year consolidated elections [S7]
In 2017 took responsibility for 125 uncounted 2016 ballots and changed drop-box procedures [S4][S5]

experience.basis: Incumbent since 2015 with 36 years in county auditor's offices, 25 in elections administration.
